mainTopic: Does קידושין from an outsider take effect on a יבמה? The views of רב and שמואל, רב's statement about קידושין and נשואין, and the sages' vote with its proof from a משנה.
overview: רב learns from a פסוק that if an outside man does קידושין with a יבמה, it does not take effect at all. שמואל is unsure what the פסוק means, so to be safe he says she needs a גט. אמימר rules like שמואל. The גמרא then works out the practical result so that the sinner does not gain: when the יבם is a regular ישראל, the outsider gives a גט and she stays permitted to the יבם. A second statement of רב, that a יבמה has no קידושין but does have נשואין, is challenged, and the גמרא gives three ways to explain it. רבי ינאי reports that the sages voted that קידושין does not take effect on a יבמה. רבי יוחנן supports this from a משנה, and רבי ינאי praises the find. ריש לקיש argues that the משנה might follow only רבי עקיבא. The גמרא pushes back, citing רבי עקיבא's view that a person can transfer something not yet in existence, and begins quoting a משנה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב: betrothal does not take effect on a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רב learns from a פסוק that קידושין by an outsider does not take effect on a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: How do we know that קידושין does not take effect on a יבמה? The פסוק says, "The wife of the dead man shall not be married outside to a strange man." This means she cannot "become" married to an outsider at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב states a rule: if an outside man tries to do קידושין with a יבמה, nothing happens. He brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה is tied to her dead husband's brother (the יבם) until ייבום or חליצה. רב reads "לא תהיה" as "there is no הויה," meaning a marriage to an outsider cannot even begin. So it is not just forbidden; it is legally empty.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
A widow whose husband died childless; she is tied to his brother
An outsider, someone not from the family

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the סוגיא: is the פסוק a total block on קידושין, or just an איסור?

phrases.english: Rav said: From where do we know
that betrothal does not take effect on a yevama?
As it says: "The wife of the dead man shall not be
married outside to a strange man"
She shall have no "becoming" married to an outsider
phrases.notes: רב is reading "לא תהיה" as "no הויה": a marriage to an outsider can't even start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בִּיבָמָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין by an outsider does not take effect on a יבמה, learned from "לא תהיה אשת המת החוצה לאיש זר."

steps.title: שמואל: she needs a get
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that because we are unsure, the יבמה needs a גט from the outsider.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: In our poverty of understanding, she needs a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב in practice. He says the outsider's קידושין might work, so she needs a גט to be released from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not say the קידושין definitely works. He admits he is unsure ("in our poverty"), and because of that doubt he is strict and requires a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: In our poverty, meaning our limited understanding

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the קידושין certainly works. He requires a גט only because of a doubt.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: In our poverty
phrases.notes: He means: we don't fully understand this פסוק, so we can't be sure.

phrases.english: she needs a bill of divorce

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב: because of doubt, a גט is required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of doubt, a יבמה who received קידושין from an outsider needs a גט.

steps.title: Explaining שמואל's doubt about the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שמואל was unsure whether the פסוק is just an איסור or a total block on קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל was unsure about this פסוק, "The wife of the dead man shall not be." Does it come to teach a לאו (a prohibition)? Or does it come to teach that קידושין does not take hold of her at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל said "in our poverty." He had two possible ways to read the פסוק and could not decide between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is only a לאו, the outsider sinned, but his קידושין still works, so she needs a גט. If it means the קידושין cannot take hold, as רב says, no גט is needed. Since שמואל is unsure, he takes the strict side.

phrases.english: Shmuel was in doubt
about this: "The wife of the dead man shall not be"
whether it comes to teach a prohibition
phrases.notes: In this reading, it's forbidden but it still works, like many sins that still take legal effect.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִדּוּשִׁין הוּא דַּאֲתָא
phrases.english: or whether it comes to teach that betrothal does not take hold of her

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind שמואל's statement in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל's doubt is whether the פסוק is a plain לאו or means that קידושין cannot take effect.

steps.title: אמימר rules like שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בר רחל reports to רב אשי that אמימר ruled the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי בר רחל said to רב אשי: This is what אמימר said: The הלכה is like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: A practical ruling is reported: in this מחלוקת we follow שמואל, so the יבמה needs a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the practical הלכה. Next, רב אשי will work out what this ruling means for a real case.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice the הלכה follows שמואל: the outsider's קידושין is treated as possibly valid, so a גט is needed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל לְרַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Rav Mari bar Rachel said to Rav Ashi
Thus said Ameimar
The halacha is like Shmuel

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: הֲלָכָה כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows שמואל: a יבמה who received קידושין from an outsider needs a גט.

steps.title: רב אשי: if the יבם is a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי draws a practical result: if the יבם is a כהן, he does חליצה, and she is permitted to the man who betrothed her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Now that אמימר said the הלכה is like שמואל, if her יבם was a כהן, he does חליצה with her, and she is permitted to the man who betrothed her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי applies שמואל's view to a specific case, where the יבם is a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the outsider's קידושין counts and he must give a גט, she now has the status of a divorcee. A כהן may not marry a divorcee, so ייבום is out, and the כהן does חליצה. That frees her from the יבם, and she becomes permitted to the man who betrothed her.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest; he may not marry a divorcee
Performs חליצה, the ceremony that frees a יבמה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר אַמֵּימָר
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Now that Ameimar said
the halacha is like Shmuel
if her yavam was a kohen
he does chalitza with her, and she is permitted to him
phrases.notes: "Him" here is the outsider who betrothed her, not the יבם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר אַמֵּימָר הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies אמימר's ruling to the case of a יבם who is a כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the יבם is a כהן, he does חליצה, and she is permitted to the man who betrothed her.

steps.title: Objection: a sinner would gain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: then the outsider would end up benefiting from his forbidden קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But she gains from this! If so, we find a sinner being rewarded!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's rule. Under it, the man who did a forbidden act gets exactly what he wanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outsider did קידושין with a יבמה, which he should not have done. Under רב אשי's rule, that act forces the כהן into חליצה and frees her to marry the outsider. The rule that a חוטא should not be נשכר means the הלכה would not set things up this way.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner who profits from his sin

phrases.english: She has really gained!
phrases.notes: Through the forbidden קידושין, she ends up free to marry the man she wanted.

phrases.english: If so, we find a sinner gaining!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's rule from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's ruling that she becomes permitted to the man who betrothed her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה does not let a sinner benefit from his sin, but this ruling rewards the outsider's forbidden קידושין.

steps.title: Corrected rule: if the יבם is a regular ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's statement is restated: if the יבם is a ישראל, the second man gives a גט, and she is permitted to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if her יבם was a regular ישראל, the second man gives her a גט, and she is permitted to the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces רב אשי's teaching with a version that does not reward the sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular ישראל may marry a divorcee. So after the outsider gives a גט, the יבם can still do ייבום, and she goes back to the family she is tied to. The outsider gains nothing, which answers the objection.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, used to restate the teaching
A regular Jew, not a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Following שמואל, the outsider must give a גט. The practical result is taught for a יבם who is a ישראל, who may still marry her, so the sinner never benefits.

phrases.english: Rather, if her yavam was a regular Israelite
the second one gives her a bill of divorce
phrases.notes: "The second one" is the outsider who betrothed her.

phrases.english: and she is permitted to him
phrases.notes: Here "him" is the יבם, who may marry a divorcee because he isn't a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 6 by restating רב אשי's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the teaching for a different case (יבם who is a ישראל instead of a כהן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching was about a כהן יבם, which lets her marry the outsider.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching is about a ישראל יבם: the outsider gives a גט, and she stays permitted to the יבם.

steps.title: רב: a יבמה has no betrothal but does have marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted through a chain, says that קידושין does not take effect on a יבמה, but נשואין does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב חייא בר יוסף, who said in the name of רב: A יבמה cannot be betrothed by another man, but marriage to him does take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב about an outsider who tries to marry a יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב splits the two stages of marriage. He says the first stage (קידושין) does not take effect on a יבמה, but the full marriage (נשואין) does. This sounds strange, and the next step will challenge it.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died without children; she waits for his brother (the יבם)
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said
that Rav Chiyya bar Yosef said
that Rav said:
A yevama: betrothal does not apply to her,
but marriage does apply to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement on the same topic of an outsider betrothing a יבמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין does not take effect on a יבמה, but נשואין does.

steps.title: If betrothal fails, marriage should fail too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the weaker stage does not work, the stronger stage should not work either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If betrothal does not take effect on her, then marriage should not take effect either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's statement as illogical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נשואין is built on top of קידושין. If the base stage cannot take effect, it makes no sense for the full marriage to take effect.

phrases.english: If betrothal does not apply to her,
marriage also should not apply to her!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קִדּוּשִׁין אֵין בָּהּ נִשּׂוּאִין נָמֵי אֵין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of רב's split in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that נשואין works while קידושין does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נשואין is a stronger stage than קידושין, so if the weaker stage fails, the stronger one must fail too.

steps.title: Fix the wording: neither betrothal nor marriage applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of רב's statement: neither קידושין nor נשואין takes effect on a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: neither betrothal nor marriage takes effect on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by changing the wording of רב's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining the strange version, the גמרא simply corrects it. The corrected version says no form of marriage to an outsider works on a יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (a signal that the wording is being corrected)

phrases.english: Say instead:
neither betrothal nor marriage applies to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by fixing the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב said נשואין takes effect on a יבמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב really meant that neither קידושין nor נשואין takes effect.

steps.title: Second answer: 'marriage' means forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: 'נשואין applies' means that if she has relations with another man, it affects her, as רב המנונא taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: what does 'marriage applies to her' mean? It means relations outside of marriage, as רב המנונא taught. A woman waiting for her יבם who had relations with another man becomes forbidden to her יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that keeps רב's wording but explains it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'נשואין' does not mean a real marriage. It means that living with another man changes her status. Following רב המנונא, such relations make her forbidden to the יבם, even though קידושין itself had no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
A woman waiting for her יבם

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What is the meaning of "marriage does apply to her"?
It refers to licentious relations, like Rav Hamnuna's teaching.
For Rav Hamnuna said:
a woman waiting for her yavam who had licentious relations
is forbidden to her yavam.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מַאי נִשּׂוּאִין יֵשׁ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא of step 9 without changing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נשואין means a real marriage that takes effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: נשואין means relations with another man, which forbid her to the יבם, as רב המנונא taught.

steps.title: Third answer: marriage needs a גט so people won't confuse cases
steps.stepSummary: A third answer keeps the original wording. After נשואין he must give a גט, because people might confuse this with a woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really it is as we said at first. Betrothal does not take effect, but marriage does, in the sense that he must give a גט. Otherwise people would confuse this case with a woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the original wording and gives a third explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נשואין does not truly take effect. The rabbis still require a גט after a public marriage. Otherwise people might wrongly think a woman who remarried after hearing her husband died overseas also needs no גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (returns to the first idea)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'נשואין יש בה' does not mean the marriage is real. It only means the rabbis require a גט because of how it looks.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually, it is as we said at first:

phrases.aramaic: קִדּוּשִׁין אֵין בָּהּ, נִשּׂוּאִין יֵשׁ בָּהּ.
phrases.english: betrothal does not apply to her, but marriage does apply to her.
Because it could be confused
with a woman whose husband went overseas.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves this unsaid: after a marriage he has to give her a גט, so people don't mix up the two cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא לְעוֹלָם כְּדַאֲמַרַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the קשיא of step 9 that keeps רב's original wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree (a גט required because of how things look)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נשואין truly takes effect on a יבמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: נשואין does not truly take effect. A גט is required so people won't confuse this with a woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers to רב: (1) fix the wording so nothing takes effect; (2) 'נשואין' means relations that forbid her to the יבם; (3) a גט is needed after נשואין so people won't mix up cases.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: the sages voted that betrothal does not work on a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי reports that the group of sages took a vote and decided that קידושין does not take effect on a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: In the group of sages, they counted votes and decided that betrothal by another man does not take effect on a יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new report: a formal vote of the sages on our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vote rules clearly that an outsider's קידושין has no effect at all on a יבמה, in line with רב's view in step 1. The next steps ask whether a משנה already teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: A group of sages learning together

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
In the group, they counted and concluded:
betrothal does not take effect with a yevama.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי בַּחֲבוּרָה נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement on the same topic, ruling clearly that קידושין does not work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין by an outsider does not take effect on a יבמה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: isn't this already in a משנה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks why a vote was needed, since a משנה already teaches that betrothal 'after your יבם does חליצה' does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: My teacher, isn't this already taught in our משנה? We learned: if a man says to a woman, 'You are betrothed to me after I convert,' 'after you convert,' 'after I am freed,' 'after you are freed,' 'after your husband dies,' 'after your sister dies,' or 'after your יבם does חליצה with you,' she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges the need for the sages' vote. He shows that a משנה already says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists cases where the woman is not yet available to this man, and in each one the קידושין fails. One case is a יבמה before חליצה. That shows a יבמה cannot be betrothed by an outsider, so why was a vote needed?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
My teacher, isn't this our mishna?
As we learned: one who says to a woman:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in בבא מציעא 16b.

phrases.english: "You are hereby betrothed to me after I convert,"
"after you convert," "after I am freed,"
"after you are freed," "after your husband dies,"
"after your sister dies,"
or "after your yavam performs chalitza with you"
she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the vote in step 13 was needed, since a משנה already teaches the same ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the sages' vote reported by רבי ינאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already rules that betrothal 'after your יבם does חליצה' fails, so the ruling was already known.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: without me lifting the shard, you would not have found the pearl
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that רבי יוחנן only saw the proof in the משנה because the ruling was told to him first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If I had not lifted the clay shard for you, would you have found the pearl under it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי answers רבי יוחנן with a picture of a pearl hidden under a shard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה was the 'pearl', but it was hidden. Only after the sages' ruling was taught could רבי יוחנן see that the משנה proves it. So the vote was still needed.
steps.whatToRemember: The sages ruled that an outsider's קידושין does not take effect on a יבמה, and רבי יוחנן found support for this in a משנה. The next step, from ריש לקיש, questions whether that משנה really proves it for everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a proof inside a משנה is often only seen after someone states the הלכה clearly.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Had I not lifted the earthenware shard for you,
would you have found the pearl beneath it?
phrases.notes: The pearl is the proof from the משנה. He means: you only found it because I told you the ruling first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the ruling was still needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה teaches it, the sages' vote added nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof in the משנה was hidden and was only noticed after the ruling was stated.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the משנה might be only רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the משנה is no real proof, because it could follow רבי עקיבא, who holds that קידושין don't take effect for those forbidden by a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: If a great man had not praised you, I would have told you that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who says betrothal does not take effect with women forbidden by a regular prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה. He says it does not prove what everyone holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה is forbidden to an outsider only by a לאו. רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין never take effect when the couple is forbidden by a לאו, so of course the משנה says her betrothal fails. But the חכמים disagree with רבי עקיבא, so under their view her קידושין might work. That means the vote was still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: People forbidden to each other by a regular לאו (not כרת)

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying the הלכה differs from the משנה. He is only saying the משנה might reflect one opinion, רבי עקיבא's, and not the view of all the חכמים.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to him (to Rabbi Yochanan):
If not for the fact that a great man praised you,
phrases.notes: The great man is רבי ינאי, from the previous step.

phrases.english: I would have said to you:
The Mishnah follows Rabbi Akiva,
who said: betrothal does not take effect
with those forbidden by a regular prohibition.
phrases.notes: A יבמה is forbidden to an outsider by this kind of plain לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: אי לאו דקלסך גברא רבה הוה אמינא לך אנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from the משנה in step 14, which רבי ינאי praised in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה proves everyone agrees קידושין don't take effect on a יבמה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה could follow only רבי עקיבא's opinion about חייבי לאוין, so it does not show what the חכמים hold.

steps.title: If it follows רבי עקיבא, the betrothal should work after the חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: under רבי עקיבא's view, betrothal set to begin after חליצה should take effect once the חליצה happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, then when he tells her 'after your יבם does חליצה for you,' the betrothal should take effect on her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's idea that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man in the משנה did not try to betroth her now. He said the betrothal should start after the חליצה, when she is no longer forbidden. רבי עקיבא's rule about חייבי לאוין should not block that. So under רבי עקיבא, the betrothal ought to work at that later time.

keyTerms.meaning: After your יבם does חליצה for you

phrases.english: And if it follows Rabbi Akiva,
when he said to her,
"After your yavam does chalitza for you,"
the betrothal should take effect on her!

steps.triggerLanguage: ואי רבי עקיבא כי אמר לה לאחר שיחלוץ ליך יבמיך ליתפסו בה קידושי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's claim in step 16 that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The betrothal in the משנה was set for after the חליצה, when the לאו no longer applies. So רבי עקיבא's rule cannot explain why it fails.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא holds a person can transfer something not yet in existence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge: רבי עקיבא holds אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם, and it begins quoting a משנה to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we have heard that רבי עקיבא says a person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world, as we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its challenge by citing a known view of רבי עקיבא. It ends with 'as we learned,' which sets up a משנה that will be quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person can transfer something that does not exist yet, he can also make a betrothal that only takes effect later. That is why, under רבי עקיבא, the betrothal 'after חליצה' should work. The proof itself comes from the משנה introduced here.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that has not yet come into existence

phrases.english: For we have heard that Rabbi Akiva
said: a person can transfer
something that has not come into the world.
As we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: The משנה is from כתובות 59a and gets quoted next.

steps.triggerLanguage: דהא שמעינן ליה לרבי עקיבא דאמר אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the basis for the challenge in step 17 and introduces a משנה as proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא holds אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in כתובות 59a, quoted next
